title: White Rice with Soy‑Based Sauce, No Added Fat

content.title: About
content.content: White rice prepared with a soy‑based sauce and no added fat is a light dish popular in Asian cuisine. The rice provides a quick source of energy, while the soy sauce adds a savory, slightly salty flavor without extra fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White rice is more refined than brown rice and contains less fiber.
Soy sauce is traditionally made by fermenting soybeans, wheat, salt, and water.
The dish is often served as a side to meat and vegetable dishes in Japan, China, and Korea.
The lack of added fat makes it suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.
Rice readily absorbs the sauce’s aroma, enhancing the overall taste.

items.title: Quick source of energy
items.content: Rice is rich in carbohydrates that are rapidly converted to glucose, providing immediate energy.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: No added fat makes the dish easy to digest and appropriate for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: While not a high‑protein food, rice contributes a modest amount of plant‑based protein.

items.title: B‑vitamin content
items.content: Rice provides thiamine (B1), niacin (B3) and folate, which support metabolic processes.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It supplies magnesium and phosphorus, important for bone health and nerve function.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White rice can cause a rapid rise in blood sugar, which may be problematic for people with diabetes.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce is salty; frequent consumption should be balanced with overall sodium intake.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to soy products.

items.title: Low fiber
items.content: Compared with whole grains, white rice provides little dietary fiber, which can affect digestion.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the rice hot, drizzling the soy sauce over it just before serving. It pairs well with steamed vegetables, lean meats, or seafood. For variety, add sliced green onions, toasted sesame seeds, or fresh ginger.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry rice in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked rice should be cooled quickly and kept in the refrigerator for no more than 2 days. Reheat to at least 75 °C before eating.
